name: Daclatasvir

overview.class: Direct-acting hepatitis C antiviral; NS5A inhibitor
uses: The October 2019 US DAKLINZA label covers chronic HCV genotype 1 or 3 infection in combination with sofosbuvir, with or without ribavirin.

paragraphs.text: The 2019 label states that daclatasvir itself requires no dose adjustment at any degree of renal impairment. It separately directs clinicians to the companion sofosbuvir and ribavirin labels; this single-agent statement does not establish the suitability of the whole regimen. Because protein binding exceeds 99%, dialysis is unlikely to substantially lower daclatasvir concentrations.

sources.citation: FDA. DAKLINZA (daclatasvir) prescribing information, revised October 2019. Application206843 supplement008. Historical US label; verified 2026-11-25.

draft_notes: Do not treat this historical label as a current HCV regimen-selection guideline. No dialysis regimen inferred. The misspelled registry entry daclastavir requires separate identity/alias review.

revision_log.change: New source-linked descriptive literature or historical US-label summary. No inferred dialysis dosing or current Philippine-label claim.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.indication: Historical October 2019 US DAKLINZA label; adult HCV genotype 1 or 3 combination therapy
usual_adult_dose.dose: 60 mg orally once daily with or without food, with sofosbuvir with or without ribavirin. Interaction-related modification and full regimen selection require the complete current product information [[DACL]]

contraindications: Strong CYP3A inducers, including rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin and St John’s wort (historical US label) [[DACL]]

serious: HBV reactivation, including liver failure and death; serious symptomatic bradycardia with amiodarone plus a sofosbuvir-containing regimen [[DACL]]

monitoring: Before treatment, test HBsAg and anti-HBc; monitor coinfected patients for HBV reactivation during and after HCV treatment (historical US label) [[DACL]]

key_interactions.action: Coadministration is not recommended in the historical label [[DACL]]

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Strong CYP3A inhibitors; moderate CYP3A inducers
